# Vendored crates

Each directory is a copy of a published crate with local fixes, used through
`[patch.crates-io]` in the workspace `Cargo.toml`. They are temporary: when
upstream publishes a release with the fix, switch back to it and delete the
copy. Check the conditions below when updating dependencies.

A copy may be switched back only when **every** item in its `PATCHES.md` (or,
for a crate without one, every item in its "Why" cell) is either present in the
upstream release with an equivalent implementation, or confirmed to be no
longer needed. Patches that change no API (limits on sizes and time, error
paths, lenient decoding) do not fail to compile when the registry version is
used, so check each one against the upstream source or a test, not only the
build. The "Switch back when" cells name the items that gate a release; they do
not replace that check, and the patch list lives only in `PATCHES.md`.

| Crate | Base | Why | Switch back when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gpui` | 0.2.2 | **Not built by the application since the GPUI migration (#1081).** The application uses `gpui-pre` 0.3.12 (the rows below); this 0.2.2 copy stays as the reference the patches were re-applied from and for its Linux clipboard unit test in CI. Delete it once nothing needs that reference. Windows IME keys, Linux decorations, atlas reuse and more; see `gpui/PATCHES.md` | Every item in `gpui/PATCHES.md` is in the GPUI release or no longer needed (including running quit handlers on Windows `WM_ENDSESSION`). Moot once the copy is deleted |
| `gpui-pre` | 0.3.12 | The `queue` and Wayland `layer_shell` modules are also compiled on `freebsd` (#1081); `InputHandler::prefers_direct_input` (direct-input fields detach the IME), `App::on_quit_request`, `Menu::menu_type` phrase-aware wrapping (`StyledText::with_wrap_joins`) and hoverable link tooltips (`InteractiveText::hoverable_tooltip`). See `gpui-pre/PATCHES.md`. The other patches are re-applied later (`spec/gpui-kit-migration-2026-11-18.md`) | Every item in `gpui-pre/PATCHES.md` is in the `gpui-pre` release or no longer needed. The release must at least build on FreeBSD and have `prefers_direct_input`, `on_quit_request` and `Menu::menu_type` |
| `gpui-pre-windows`, `gpui-pre-macos`, `gpui-pre-linux` | 0.3.12 | Direct-input fields (#1081): Windows drops the commit that ends the composition when the IME is detached, macOS limits the input sources to Roman, Wayland asks `query_ime_enabled`; macOS `applicationShouldTerminate:` and the Window menu type; Windows `IsWindow` before teardown and no simulated Alt when our own window is in front; clipboard limits (32 MiB pipe reads and a cancellable background Wayland read with a 5 second deadline, 16 MiB Windows text). See each `PATCHES.md` | Switch each crate back only with the matching `gpui-pre` release, and only when every item in its own `PATCHES.md` is in that release or no longer needed, including the clipboard size and time limits (Linux, Windows) |
| `rav1d` | 1.1.0 | A damaged AV1 stream can reach an `unwrap` in an error path of `dav1d_send_data` (`extern "C"`, cannot unwind), which aborts the process; AVIF previews decode untrusted files with it (D018). Without the unused assembly; see `rav1d/PATCHES.md` | Every item in `rav1d/PATCHES.md` is in the `rav1d` release or no longer needed. For the abort, the release no longer aborts on the data of `crates/media/tests/avif_mutations.rs` (run it with a large `AVIF_MUTATIONS`) |
| `zed-xim` | 0.4.0-zed | Lenient COMPOUND_TEXT decoding instead of panics (IBus/Mozc), XIM input style selection, bounded data property atoms | Every item in this row and in the "Local zed-xim" section of `gpui/PATCHES.md` is in the `zed-xim` release or no longer needed: it decodes COMPOUND_TEXT without panicking and bounds the atoms, and the style selection moves back into GPUI |
| `irc-proto` | 1.1.0 | `LineCodec` rejects lines over 16 KiB (`MAX_LINE_BYTES`); upstream buffers a line without limit. Its `encoding` feature uses `encoding_rs` instead of the unmaintained `encoding` crate (RUSTSEC-2021-0153), and the workspace enables it directly rather than through `irc`'s `encoding` feature. `charsets` lets the codec convert the text of a `PRIVMSG`/`NOTICE` to a given target with another encoding than the rest of the line (per-channel `/charset`, #396). `LineCodec::encode` drops a line holding CR, LF or NUL besides the final `\r\n`, so no line, including the `irc` crate's own PONG and CTCP replies, can inject a command (#554). `line::is_single_line` is public so irc-core's transcript uses the same check (#573) | Every item in this row is in the `irc-proto` release or no longer needed: the line length limit, the maintained charset crate (`irc`'s `encoding` feature must then no longer pull in `encoding`), per-target `charsets`, the CR/LF/NUL check in `LineCodec::encode` and the public `line::is_single_line` |
| `irc` | 1.1.0 | A received KICK of our own nickname drops the channel's `channel-lists` entry, like a PART we send does (`src/client/mod.rs`). "Our own nickname" is the one the server confirmed (RPL_WELCOME, then our own NICK), not `current_nickname()`, which ignores later nick changes. `Client::forget_channel_list` lets irc-core drop the list when its own casemapping-aware check sees the KICK, because the built-in check is ASCII-only (`nick{1}` vs `nick[1]`). Upstream only removed the kicked user, so a rejoin appended to stale entries: modes went to the old entry, members who left meanwhile stayed, and `list_channels()` still reported the channel (#342). A list exists only for a channel we joined: our own JOIN creates it empty (dropping an old one) and a NAMES reply for any other channel is ignored (upstream tracked it without limit). The first NAMES line after an end of NAMES (366) rebuilds the list and a nickname is listed once, so PART, QUIT and MODE reach it after a repeated NAMES (#597). Only the first end of MOTD (376/422) of a connection joins the configured channels; later ones join nothing, and the JOIN of every tracked channel is gone (#597). Member lists are bounded (50,000 members and 16 MiB per channel; 100,000 members, 32 MiB and 2,000 channels per connection; a NICK that lengthens an entry counts too; an entry counts its strings and 128 bytes, kept in a ledger updated by each list change; a refreshed or shrunk list gives back its capacity and a `User` keeps each access level once): NAMES, JOIN or NICK over a limit returns the new `Error::ChannelListLimit`, which ends the connection (#677). The `body-charsets` feature adds `Config::body_charsets`, handed to the line codec for per-channel text encodings (#396) The outgoing queue (`src/client/queue.rs`) holds at most 1024 messages and 1 MiB; upstream's was unbounded, so a server that sent `PING` faster than the socket drained piled up automatic `PONG`s. Every send, automatic replies included, passes the limit, and a full queue fails with `Error::OutgoingQueueFull` (`QUIT` alone is always admitted so it is written behind a backlog), which ends the connection like any stream error (#678). The clock reads (the keepalive `PING` data, the CTCP `PING` and the `TIME` reply) use `jiff` instead of the unmaintained `chrono` (RUSTSEC-2026-0543, #1068) | `Client` is no longer used (#266), or every item in this row (KICK and channel list handling, member and queue limits, `body_charsets`, `jiff` clock reads) is in an upstream release or no longer needed; upstream 1.1.0 is the latest release and has none of them |

`irc` and `rav1d` set `[lints.rust] warnings = "allow"` in their
`Cargo.toml`: their upstream code has unused items and old idioms that Cargo
would hide in a crates.io dependency, and fixing them here would only widen
the difference from upstream. Keep local fixes warning-free all the same.

Run the copies' own tests with `cargo test -p zed-xim` and
`cargo test -p irc-proto` (CI does both on Linux).

The `irc` copy is not a workspace member (its examples and dev-dependencies
are not vendored), so `cargo test -p irc` does not run here. To run its unit
tests, copy `vendor/irc` and `vendor/irc-proto` into a scratch directory, drop
the `[[example]]` tables, add an empty `[workspace]` and a `[patch.crates-io]`
entry for `irc-proto`, then run
`cargo test --no-default-features --features channel-lists,ctcp,tls-rust`.
